title: hybrid-observability-sequencer-and-hook-adapter
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Background: Dedicated and Private deployments use on-prem/VPC collectors that sometimes reorder, drop, or duplicate telemetry during transient network partitions and upgrades. Existing collector relays do best-effort forwarding which makes cross-tenant correlation, ordered trace reassembly, and accurate latency dashboards unreliable for Private/Dedicated customers.

Goal: Implement a hybrid "Sequencer + Hook Adapter" layer that lives in the perimeter/edge (per-deployment relay) to provide: (1) stable ordered ingestion for traces and metrics with per-tenant watermarks, (2) a lightweight trace-hook adapter that standardizes hooks for gRPC/HTTP services (server interceptors) across Private and Dedicated runtimes, and (3) an atomic batch-ack mechanism so upstream collectors can deterministically replay without cross-tenant duplication. The feature must preserve tenant isolation guarantees and be opt-in per deployment.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change downstream storage schemas, long-term retention policy, or user-facing SDK surface beyond adding a compatible hook adapter that is backwards-compatible with existing trace headers.

Why different from prior work: Prior tickets focused on sampling, coarse tenant fencing, or collector sharding. This design introduces a logical sequencer on the relay with vector-clock-ish watermarks per tenant and an 'envelope signing' step for ephemeral replay tokens to prevent cross-tenant replay attacks in shared ingress gateways. It also includes histogram-normalization for metrics before ingestion so latency percentiles are meaningful across private collectors with different bucket layouts.
acceptance_criteria: Sequencer component deployed behind a feature flag for two Dedicated customers and one Private test cluster
Traces contain a sequencer watermark header and are reassembled in correct order at ingest layer 99.9% of the time under simulated partitioning (chaos tests)
Collector-to-relay batch-ack protocol implemented with idempotent replay token; replayed batches are de-duped downstream
Trace-hook adapter libraries (Go and Python) published to internal package registry with examples and automated integration test using envoy + onprem collector
Latency/error dashboards show stable percentile curves and separate tenant vs infrastructure latency breakdowns in Console for the test deployments
Security review completed and envelope signing uses existing KMS integration for private deployments
tech_notes: Sequencer design: maintain per-tenant monotonically-increasing watermark (uint64) + per-collector local counter to avoid cross-tenant collisions

Backpressure strategy: sequencer writes to local WAL and returns 202 when fast path accepted; collectors poll for batch ack; if WAL grows > threshold we shed low-priority telemetry (metrics over traces) and emit quota events
Replay token: ephemeral HMAC(envelope || sequencer-watermark) signed with deployment-specific key; token TTL 10m for Hosted/Dedicated, configurable for Private
Metrics normalization: convert incoming histograms to a canonical bucket set using interpolation to avoid percentiles being skewed by bucket boundaries from different SDK versions

Hook adapter: provide server and client interceptors that attach original trace ids, sequencer-watermark stub, and detect local sampling overrides; fall back to existing header format when adapter absent
Operational signals: track sequencer queue depth, WAL bytes, batch-ack latency, reassembly error rate, and token-sign failures; create SLO alerts for >0.5% reassembly errors over 10m
Data plane compatibility: sequencer must be transparent for customers not opting in; use capability handshake during TLS mutual-auth to negotiate sequencing features
Security: envelope signing uses customer-managed KMS for Private; dedicated keys per-customer to prevent cross-tenant replay
